1. Scavenging System

A scavenging system must be used to remove Nitrous Oxide (N₂O) from the patient’s mask.

Exhaust ventilation of N₂O from the patient's mask should be maintained at an airflow rate of 45 LPM.

The airflow must be measured using a calibrated flow device.

The exhaust gas must be vented outdoors and must not be discharged into the room ventilation system.

2. Room Ventilation

Where possible, 100% fresh outdoor air should be used for dental operatory ventilation.

Supply and exhaust vents should be placed well apart to ensure proper air circulation.

Vent placement must prevent short-circuiting of airflow and allow effective mixing of fresh air.

3. Auxiliary Exhaust Ventilation

A local exhaust hood should be installed near the patient’s mouth.

This hood helps capture excess Nitrous Oxide (N₂O) released during breathing.

• Intended for removal of existing root canal filling materials such as gutta-percha and sealers.
• Used for canal shaping during endodontic retreatment procedures.

2. Instructions for Use

• Establish straight-line access to the root canal prior to instrumentation.
• Select the appropriate file size according to canal anatomy and clinical requirement.
• Operate the file using a gentle in-and-out (pecking) motion.
• Use recommended motor settings as specified for the file system.
• Irrigate thoroughly between each file to remove debris and softened filling material.
• Continue sequential instrumentation until complete removal of filling material and desired canal shaping is achieved.

3. Recommended Motor Settings

• Speed: 300–500 RPM
• Torque: 2.0–3.5 Ncm (or as recommended by the manufacturer)

4. Precautions

• Do not force the file or apply excessive apical pressure.
• Maintain adequate irrigation and lubrication during use.
• Discard files showing signs of wear, deformation, or unwinding.
• Always use rubber dam isolation during the procedure.

5. Sterilization

• Files may be supplied sterile or non-sterile depending on the manufacturer.
• If non-sterile, autoclave at 134°C for 3–5 minutes before use.
• Single-use is recommended to reduce the risk of file fatigue and separation.

6. Storage

• Store in a clean and dry environment.
• Protect from moisture and corrosive substances.
description:
The Retreatment File is specially designed for efficient and safe removal of root canal filling materials during endodontic retreatment procedures. Its advanced flute design and progressive taper allow smooth penetration into obturated canals while minimizing procedural errors.

The file features a non-cutting safety tip, which helps reduce ledge formation, apical extrusion, and canal transportation. Sharp cutting flutes ensure high cutting efficiency for removing gutta-percha and sealers in a controlled manner. Precise length markings provide better working-length control and enhanced clinical accuracy.

Q: How does a retreatment file work?
A: It uses super-elastic and shape-memory properties of niti to flexibly negotiate curved or narrow root canals while applying cutting forces to remove existing filling materials like gutta-percha and sealers.

Q: What are the primary uses of a retreatment file?
A: It is used for removal of gutta-percha, carrier-based obturations, retreatment of previously treated root canals, and negotiation of curved or blocked canals during retreatment procedures.

Q: How should a retreatment file be used for best results?
A: Use it with a compatible rotary endodontic handpiece at recommended rpm and torque; begin with coronal flaring, gently introduce the file to the working length under continuous irrigation, and employ a brushing motion to effectively remove filling material.

Q: What are the safety precautions when using a retreatment file?
A: Do not apply excessive lateral force, discard the file if bent, fractured, or showing signs of metal fatigue, and use only by trained dental professionals following sterilization protocols.

Q: Can the retreatment files be sterilized for reuse?
A: Yes, the files are autoclavable and should be sterilized according to clinic protocols, such as a 134°c autoclave cycle, and inspected carefully before each use.

Q: What benefits does using a retreatment file provide?

short_description:
A dental abutment is a small component that connects the implant fixture (the part embedded in the jawbone) to the final prosthesis — a crown, bridge, or denture.
A “regular” (or “standard/straight”) abutment is a prefabricated, off-the-shelf abutment designed for typical implant placements where no special angulation or custom shape is needed. On DentalKart, these are listed under their Implant Prosthetics/Implant Abutment section.

Material: Manufactured from Grade 5 Titanium (Ti-6Al-4V) offering high strength, corrosion resistance, and proven biocompatibility.

Compatibility: Designed for 4.0 mm implant platforms and compatible with major implant systems; confirm system interface prior to ordering.

Sterilization & Packaging: Supplied in sterile, single-use packaging. Follow clinic protocol for handling; do not use if the sterile barrier is damaged.

Dimensions & Tolerances: Outer diameter 4.0 mm, height 10.5 mm (1.05 cm). Manufacturing tolerances ±0.02 mm to ensure consistent prosthetic fit.

Manufacturer & Warranty: Produced by DentalTech Labs. Includes 1-year warranty against manufacturing defects when used according to instructions.
key_specifications:
Connection type (internal vs external; conical vs platform-match, etc)	Determines how the abutment locks to the implant; affects stability and risk of micro-gap or screw loosening. 
Material (Titanium, Titanium-alloy, Zirconia/ceramic, etc.)	Affects strength, biocompatibility, and aesthetics. Titanium is strong and durable; ceramic/zirconia gives better esthetics but lower strength. 
Abutment height / gingival cuff height	Needs to match tissue thickness so crown emerges properly from gum. Incorrect height can compromise gum health or aesthetics.
directions:

Ensure the implant has fully osseointegrated and the site is clean and free of debris.

Position the abutment onto the implant connection and ensure proper alignment.

Use the recommended torque wrench.

Typical torque: 25–30 Ncm (depending on manufacturer guidelines).

Verify Fit

Check stability and confirm that the abutment is fully seated with no rotation.

Proceed with Prosthetic Restoration

Take impression (if required) or place the final crown/bridge after lab fabrication.

other_info:
Direction to Use: Preparation:

Turn off the cooling water and atomization switches.

Select a suitable lifter based on the position of the patient's extracted teeth.

Connect the dental pneumatic source connector to the universal connector of the dental treatment machine, ensuring a tight fit.

Installation:

Grip the handle firmly with one hand.

Align the tail of the head with the link hole and insert it while turning slightly until the head is in position. The head should not rotate freely.

Loosen the tappet lock sleeve to allow it to reset automatically.

Ensure that the push-pull head has a slight range of movement but remains securely in place.

Debugging:

Confirm that the cooling water and atomization gas switches are off.

Step on the pedal to test the pneumatics, checking for normal operation.

Inspect the connection for any leaks at the gas source connection head.

Verify that the air pressure indicator reads above 0.3 MPa during operation; adjust if necessary.

Operation:

Use the pen-shaped handle to position the sharp edge of the blade in the periodontal space, ensuring the blade plane is aligned with the teeth.

Step on the pedal to wedge the sharp edge to a depth of approximately 1.2 mm.

Rotate the tappet within a small range to increase the gap. Ensure the tappet remains centered in the periodontal gap.

other_info:
Direction for Use: Preparation:

Ensure the root canal is prepared and dried using a paper point. Do not dry completely, as the material sets with moisture.

Application Methods:

Conventional Method:

Dispense the paste on a mixing pad. Use a Gutta Percha point to carry the paste into the canal, ensuring complete coverage.

Tip Delivery Technique:

Attach the disposable plastic intracanal tip to the syringe. Dispense the paste directly into the coronal third of the canal, using the plunger to push the paste into place. Utilize a dental file or Gutta Percha point to coat the canal walls. If using the condensation method, place another Gutta Percha point coated with sealer and complete obturation. Cut excess Gutta Percha at the orifice with a heat source and remove excess sealer from the chamber with wet cotton swabs.

Filling of Canal:

For filling the canal space independently, ensure to prevent extrusion of the material. Use a barrier at the apex to avoid overfilling.

Post-Application:

Avoid overfilling to prevent extrusion. In case of accidental extrusion into the mandibular canal, remove the material promptly.

Precautions:

Avoid contact with eyes and skin. In case of contact, rinse immediately with water and seek medical attention if irritation occurs. Do not swallow or ingest. In the event of accidental swallowing, drink water and seek medical advice if nausea or illness develops.

Ensure the handpiece is compatible with your E-type micromotor.

Check the handpiece for any visible damage before every use.

Clean the exterior surface with a soft cloth and approved disinfectant.

Verify proper functioning of fiber optic light and quattro water spray.

2. Bur Insertion

Press the push-button  firmly.

Insert a Ø1.60 mm FG bur (recommended bur length 25 mm, chucking length 11.6 mm).

Release the push button and gently pull the bur to confirm it is securely locked.

Attach the handpiece to the E-type micromotor.

Ensure the connection is tight and secure to avoid vibration or leakage.

Always start at low speed and increase gradually.

Maintain adequate water spray to cool the bur and prevent overheating.

Avoid applying excessive pressure—let the bur do the cutting.

Ensure clear visibility by checking fiber optic illumination.

5. After Use

Remove the bur by pressing the push button only after the handpiece stops rotating completely.

Disconnect the handpiece from the micromotor.

Wipe the exterior surface to remove debris and bio-contamination.

Brush off visible debris using a soft brush.

Rinse under running water—do not immerse the entire handpiece in disinfectants.

Allow the handpiece to cool completely before reuse.

Avoid dropping or exposing the handpiece to excessive heat or moisture.

Keep away from corrosive chemicals.

Always use high-quality FG burs to prevent breakage.

Never operate without water spray to avoid thermal damage.

Inspect the handpiece regularly for abnormal noise, vibration, or reduced water flow.
